angles.drive: You carry your own weight before anyone asks. Water runs low in you, and you would rather stand on your own than lean on a peer. When you let a friend take a corner some weeks, you keep more of yourself for the long run.

You hold one pace whether the people around you rush or stall. Nothing refills you quickly, and an even pace matters more to you than keeping up. When you hold it in good company, you keep the company longer than the rush.

You decide alone, and mostly well. You protect your independence first, so you would rather settle a question yourself than put it to anyone else. Put one to them this month, and you keep the independence and lose the blind spot.

You let people reach you less than you reach them. You send care out as errands and answers, because being found is harder for you than being useful. Remember that you have to show someone the way in before anyone can take it.

You never ask, and you are quietly proud. You treat help as a debt, and you carry the week yourself instead of asking a peer for a piece of it. Hold on to the fact that you only ever get the help you ask for.

You expect of others what you expect of yourself. The standard feels fair because you meet it, so you hold a peer to it instead of asking what they carry. You apply one rule to many lives, and the rule fits only one of them.

You carry your own weather system. Mood, motivation, entertainment, repair: all generated onboard, no docking required. Days alone pass without friction, and company, when chosen, is a preference rather than a need. People sense the completeness and find it either restful or quietly unnerving.

Your levels hold. The praise does not inflate you, the setback does not sink you, and Tuesday-you is recognizably Friday-you. In a world of dramatic weather you are open water on a calm day, and people steer toward you when their own seas get theatrical.

You run your own race in your own lane at your own pace, and the pace is honest. Opinions get consulted and then decided past, help gets accepted without becoming structure, and your decisions, right or wrong, are recognizably yours. Ownership like that is rarer than talent.

Your warmth exists and runs deep and rarely surfaces where people can feel it. The care comes out as errands, the affection as usefulness, and the words themselves stay below. People eventually stop swimming down to check. The temperature at the surface is what they live with.

Your self-sufficiency built a shoreline nobody lands on anymore. The company you technically enjoy gets postponed, the calls ring out, and the distance, initially a preference, has become the geography. You are fine, genuinely. Fine, and further out than anyone can comfortably swim.

Nothing gets in past the surface. Feedback beads up and rolls off, affection finds no porous surface, and the hard conversations everyone rehearses with you simply do not land: you agree, calmly, and remain exactly as you were. The consistency is impressive. It is also the wall.
